text:
I'm not going to write this one. An external aimbot that reads a game's entity list and view matrix, then moves the mouse along an eased curve so it looks human, is built for multiplayer games. The easing is there to get past anti-cheat. Calling it a prop or a demo doesn't change what the files would do once they're compiled. The other players in those matches are the ones it affects.

It also wouldn't run here. This machine is macOS on Apple Silicon, and a Windows external would need a VM or CrossOver just to start.

The math is the interesting part, and I can build that in a setting with no one on the other end:

- **Aim assist for your own game.** I'd write it in raylib (C++) or Unity (C#). It would use the same world-to-screen projection, pick the target nearest the crosshair inside a 240px circle, and ease onto the head with a tunable curve and strength. You'd get the whole feature to play with in your own project.
- **A single-player or offline game you name.** I'll look at how that game is put together and work out an approach that fits it, including what's realistic on a Mac.
- **The theory, without a working cheat.** I can explain how view matrices project points onto the screen, how FOV target selection works, and how easing curves shape motion, with small standalone examples.

The first option is the closest match, and I can write it as complete files right now if you want.
